question:
A pregnant woman at 30 weeks' gestation (G1P0) is evaluated in the emergency department for acute
abdominal pain. For the past 3 weeks, she has felt unwell and noticed decreased fetal movement and
less-than-expected abdominal growth. On examination, she appears restless and diaphoretic, with vital
signs showing BP 90/60 mm Hg, pulse 115/min, and respiratory rate 12/min. Ultrasound reveals fetal
demise. Laboratory results indicate: - Hemoglobin: 10.3 g/dL - Platelets: 50,000/µL - PT: 25 seconds -
PTT: 55 seconds What should be the immediate next step in management? Answer Choices: (A) IV
fluids (B) Immediate hysterectomy (C) Blood transfusion (D) Fresh frozen plasma (E) Emergency
cesarean delivery (F) Platelet transfusion (G) Initiation of labor (H) Magnesium sulfate infusion (I)
Administration of corticosteroids (J) Vasopressor support
 A. Administration of corticosteroids
B. Blood transfusion
C. Fresh frozen plasma
D. Platelet transfusion
E. Vasopressor support
F. IV fluids
G. Initiation of labor
H. Emergency cesarean delivery
I. Immediate hysterectomy
J. Magnesium sulfate infusion
